Best wearable for your day

Which all-in-one wearable is right for you?

There isn’t one best wearable breast pump. Match the job: warmth and massage, everyday pumping, a slimmer in-bra profile at work, app control with a quieter motor, or starting on a budget.

Warmth and massage

Wellness 1

Wellness 1 warms the cup and adds massage with the suction rhythm, with three warmth levels at 37°C, 39°C and 41°C. App control, so you can adjust warmth and massage from your phone.

Everyday pumping

M5 Smart

M5 Smart is the everyday wearable breast pump for most UK mums: app control, a 230 g cup, and suction up to −285 mmHg. Start here if you want an in-bra pump with a phone app and no extra hardware.

Discreet at work

Air 1

Air 1 is the slimmest all-in-one wearable at 61 mm, with a charging case for longer days out. Choose it when a lower in-bra profile matters under work clothes, especially if you’re
pumping at work
.

App control, quieter motor

M9

M9 is the quieter all-in-one wearable (≤42 dB), with app control, 15 suction levels and up to −300 mmHg. Pick it if you want finer control and a lower motor note.

Daily power, no app

M6

M6 gives up to −300 mmHg without an app. Choose it if you want a simple daily wearable and you’d rather skip Bluetooth.

Starting on a budget

S12 Pro Quick

S12 Pro Quick is the entry all-in-one wearable if you want in-bra pumping at a lower price, with a 210 ml cup and a quicker clean.

Also on this page

Separate unit, in-bra collection cups

If you want collection cups in the bra and the motor off the chest, that’s V1 Pro or V2 Pro. They’re wearable in the UK sense — just not all-in-one. The motor is a separate unit; the cups sit in-bra, with tubing.

More levels · home

V1 Pro

Hospital-strength electric, with a separate unit and in-bra collection cups. 15 suction levels and up to −300 mmHg, for longer sessions at home when you want the motor off your chest.

Light motor

V2 Pro

Hospital-strength electric, with a separate unit and in-bra collection cups. The pump head is 127 g, so the cups stay light in the bra while the motor sits outside.

Shop hospital-strength electric pumps

Know the difference

Hands-free is not the same as wearable

Hands-free only means your hands are free. What sits in the bra, and where the motor is, is the real split.

All-in-one wearable

Tube-free. Motor, flange and collector sit in the bra. On this page: Wellness 1, M5 Smart, Air 1, M9, M6, S12 Pro Quick and S9 Pro.

Hands-free

A behaviour, not a product type. A pumping bra with a tubed pump can also be hands-free. Searching “hands free breast pump” does not mean you need an all-in-one cup.

Separate unit, in-bra collection cups

Wearable, but not all-in-one: collection cups in the bra, motor outside, tubing. V1 Pro and V2 Pro. Same idea as a Freestyle- or Stride-style setup. Full
hospital-strength electric
range.

Before you buy

What to check on a wearable pump

01

Flange fit

Measure nipple diameter, not bra cup. Most Momcozy wearables include 17/19/21 mm inserts with a 24 mm flange. Pain, a white ring, or too much areola in the tunnel means resize before you turn suction up.

02

Leak-proofing

Check how the cup sits in a supportive pumping bra and whether you can lean forward a little. A poor seal is often fit or angle, not a reason to jump model.

03

How slim it sits

Air 1 is the slimmest all-in-one at 61 mm. Choose that lower profile if you’re packing
breastfeeding essentials for working mums
and need the cup to sit flatter under work clothes.

04

Cleaning

Count the parts that touch milk and how quickly you can put the cup back together. A heated cup has extra parts. A wearable you dread washing will not stay your everyday pump.

05

Warmth and massage

Wellness 1 warms the cup to 37°C, 39°C or 41°C and adds massage with the suction rhythm. Warmth uses more charge — about 6 sessions with warmth, about 10 pumping only.

If you’re still
choosing a breast pump in the UK
, start with format: a tube-free all-in-one wearable, or a separate unit with in-bra collection cups. Then pick a model from Best for, or V1 Pro / V2 Pro above.

Frequently asked questions

Wearable pump FAQs

Which wearable breast pump is best?

There isn’t one best wearable breast pump. For warmth and massage, start with Wellness 1. For everyday pumping, M5 Smart. For
working mums
who need a slimmer in-bra profile, Air 1. For app control and a quieter motor, M9. M6 skips the app. S12 Pro Quick covers a lower price. Match the job rather than chasing a single winner.

What is a hands-free breast pump?

Hands-free means you are not holding the flanges. That can be an all-in-one wearable, or a separate unit with in-bra collection cups. Hands-free is not a product type on its own.

Are V1 Pro and V2 Pro wearable pumps?

Yes. In the UK, wearable usually means the cups sit in your bra. V1 Pro and V2 Pro do that with a separate motor unit and in-bra collection cups. They are not all-in-one, tube-free wearables like M5 Smart or Air 1.
Shop hospital-strength electric pumps
if you want that format in more depth.

How should I store expressed milk in the UK?

Follow current NHS guidance. The NHS advises storing expressed milk in the fridge for up to 8 days at 4°C or lower, and in a freezer at −18°C or lower for up to 6 months. Some NHS pages also allow up to 6 hours at room temperature. Check the
NHS expressing page
before you rely on a figure.

What flange size do I need?

Measure nipple diameter, not bra cup. Most Momcozy wearables include 17/19/21 mm inserts with a 24 mm flange. Pain, a white ring on the nipple, or too much areola being pulled in means resize before you turn suction up. Fit matters more than buying a “stronger” pump.

Do wearable pumps decrease milk supply?

Not if the cup empties the breast well. Supply drops when the seal is poor, the flange is the wrong size, or sessions are too short or too infrequent — not because the motor sits in the bra. If output falls, check fit first, then session length. Speak to a midwife or lactation specialist if you’re worried about supply.

Can I exclusively use a wearable breast pump?

Yes, if it empties you comfortably and your output stays steady. Plenty of UK mums use an all-in-one wearable as their only pump. If you need longer sessions at home with the motor off the chest, V1 Pro and V2 Pro are on this page; the wider
hospital-strength electric
range is on the Electric collection.

Can I wear a regular bra while pumping?

A stretchy everyday bra can hold a cup if it is supportive enough to keep the seal. A dedicated pumping bra is more reliable for leaks and for leaning forward a little. If milk escapes, it is usually fit or angle, not a reason to jump model.

Does warmth and massage in a wearable pump help with let-down?

Some mums find in-cup warmth and a massage rhythm easier at the start of a session. Wellness 1 warms to 37°C, 39°C or 41°C. Warmth uses more battery — about 6 sessions with warmth, about 10 pumping only. It is a comfort feature, not a medical treatment. Speak to a midwife or lactation specialist if pumping is painful.
